title: 5 ways Amazon is supporting US communities in 2026, from free meals to affordable homes
summary: From disaster relief to housing and scholarships, Amazon's community investments are helping neighbors across the country.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon has donated and delivered more than 17 million essential supplies and technology in response to 90 natural disasters.


- Amazon has delivered more than 75 million meals directly to families’ doorsteps.


- Amazon has committed $2.7 billion to create or preserve affordable homes for more than 60,000 residents.


---


Since Amazon was founded, we've partnered with the people, places, and organizations that strengthen the


[communities](https://www.aboutamazon.com/impact/community) where we live and work.


Working alongside trusted community organizations and leaders, we use our


[delivery network](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/transportation/amazon-investment-delivery-network-small-town-rural-us) ,


[technology](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/technology) , and


[innovation](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/innovation) to


[deliver food](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-summer-meals-kids-rural-delivery) directly to families facing hunger,


[expand access to affordable housing](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-housing-equity-fund) , and support


[education](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/education) and skills training. When natural disasters strike, we apply the same capabilities that get packages to customers' doorsteps to


[deliver critical aid](https://www.aboutamazon.com/impact/community/disaster-relief) quickly.


[Amazon delivers more than 75 million meals to families in need](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-expands-food-access-delivery)


In 2025, Amazon extended its free home food delivery commitment through 2028 to help millions of families access food.


This work is possible through collaboration with hundreds of community partners and our own employees, who generously volunteer their time and talents to turn action into impact.


I invite you to explore the innovations and investments we've made across our headquarters in


[Washington state’s Puget Sound](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/6c/27/6944ff4c4024a3be862d5d575566/hq1-community-impact-report-final.pdf) and


[National Capital Region](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/64/53/a941409447f5ad4e3d8f94e4627d/hq2-community-impact-report-final.pdf) —and across the U.S. Here are highlights of our commitments in 2026.

1.


When disasters strike, we apply the same strengths that get packages to doorsteps every day to get critical aid where it's needed fast.[Since 2017, we’ve donated and delivered](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-helps-hurricanes-wildfires-floods) more than 17 million essential supplies and[technology](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-disaster-relief-technology-kits-recovery) in response to 90 disasters across the U.S.


We maintain[12 Disaster Relief hubs](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-disaster-relief-programs-hubs-portal) stocked with emergency supplies like tarps, blankets, and toiletries to make sure we’re ready to support communities before disasters strike around the world. This allows us to donate and deliver essential items to trusted partners such as the[American Red Cross](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/how-amazon-supports-american-red-cross) and[World Central Kitchen](https://wck.org/story/) within hours.


We stood with communities close to home when natural disasters struck[Washington state](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/washington) . When catastrophic flooding hit communities in the[Skagit Valley](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/washington-floods-amazon-communities-support) , we delivered more than 75,000 free emergency supplies and donated $3 million to support response and recovery. And when devastating wildfires forced thousands of families from their homes in[eastern Washington](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/spokane-washington-fires-amazon-disaster-relief) , we worked alongside local nonprofits to deliver more than 165,000 emergency supplies and technology systems to support relief efforts and restore connectivity.


2.


We delivered more than 75 million free meals to families in need


Amazon delivery driver loading crates of produce.


Amazon supports the critical work of our partners to help families experiencing hunger by expanding access to food. Using our fleet of trucks and vans, we transport groceries from suppliers to food banks, and from food banks to pantries, schools, and other community distribution points. In 2026 alone, we transported more than 45 million pounds of food in bulk on behalf of food bank and pantry partners.


But getting food to a distribution site is only part of the challenge. Many families struggle to get to their local food pantry because of work schedules, transportation limitations, or mobility challenges. That's why we also partner with local food banks to bring meals directly to families’ doorsteps—for free. Using Amazon’s logistics network—including[Delivery Service Partners](https://www.aboutamazon.com/impact/empowerment/delivery-partners) ,[Amazon Flex](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/amazon-flex) , and Amazon Shipping—we've delivered more than 75 million free meals to families in need since 2020.


In summer 2026, working alongside No Kid Hungry, food banks, and school districts, we[delivered 2 million meals](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-summer-meals-kids-rural-delivery) directly to students’ doorsteps in rural communities across 13 states. The program, which works with 18 food bank and school district partners, uses Amazon's rural delivery network to reach families during the summer months, when school meals are unavailable and parents’ work schedules, long distances, and limited transportation can make it difficult to access traditional distribution sites.


[How Amazon’s rapid response technology systems help communities recover faster](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-disaster-relief-technology-kits-recovery)


The systems are produced for local first responders to use in the aftermath of disasters, designed to be as simple as flipping a light switch.


3.


We created or preserved more than 27,000 affordable homes


We believe everyone should have access to housing they can afford. That’s why we created our[housing fund](https://www.aboutamazon.com/impact/community/housing-equity) , which has committed and deployed more than $2.7 billion to support housing affordability across the Puget Sound, National Capital, and Nashville regions.


As we mark five years since launching the fund in 2021, Amazon has created or preserved more than 27,000 affordable homes—positively impacting an estimated 60,000 residents across our hometown communities.


The properties we invest in are required to remain affordable for 99 years, creating generational stability for families in their communities.


4.


We supported education and skills training from classroom to career


An AWS Think Big Space classroom at River Oaks Elementary School.


Amazon is committed to[expanding access to education](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws-student-rewards-free-cloud-ai-training) and skills training that prepare students and learners for the careers of tomorrow.


In 2026, Amazon awarded 200 high school seniors with[Amazon Future Engineer scholarships](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-awards-16-million-in-college-tuition-to-u-s-computer-science-students) , providing college tuition support for the next generation of computer science and engineering talent. Since the program's inception, Amazon has awarded more than $70 million in scholarships to students across the United States.


We’re also investing in our own employees. Since 2015, more than 240,000 U.S. employees have built new skills through[Career Choice](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/career-choice) , which is Amazon’s program that provides education and training opportunities to help employees grow their careers at Amazon or elsewhere.


In our hometown communities, AWS Skills Centers have provided more than 180,000 free training and education engagements to learners in the Puget Sound and National Capital regions, helping people build skills for in-demand careers in cloud computing and other growing fields.


[Future Ready 2030: How Amazon is helping more people build skills for new careers in AI, robotics, and beyond](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-future-of-work-skills-jobs-training)


One year in, Amazon’s $2.5B Future Ready 2030 commitment is reaching students, employees, and career changers, with $1B for Career Choice and new pathways.


5.


We supported more than 2,400 local organizations with 90,000 employee volunteers


Our employees consistently turn their passion for their communities into meaningful action.


They pack supplies to support neighbors in the wake of natural disasters, build playsets for children with pediatric cancer, and help prepare meals for families in need. They also lend their professional skills through[pro bono legal services](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/policy-news-views/amazon-pro-bono-report-2026) , nonprofit consultations, and mentoring.


Amazon employees don’t just work in their[communities](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/community) —they show up for them.


In 2026, more than 90,000 Amazon volunteers brought their time, expertise, and talents to support their communities across the country.[Volunteers](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/volunteer) took part in more than 12,000 volunteer events supporting more than 2,400 local organizations.
